Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Left-ear hearing loss ongoing for about six weeks.
  - Associated tinnitus in the left ear.
  - Intermittent dizziness; no ear pain, no discharge, no fever.
  - Hearing difficulties appear unilateral (left ear); right ear hearing described as normal.
  - Some relief of tinnitus with watching TV or listening to music.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Symptoms present for ~6 weeks, on a fluctuating (intermittent) basis.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Tinnitus in left ear; unilateral hearing loss; intermittent dizziness.
  - No ear pain or discharge reported.
- Past episodes and treatments:
  - Prior hearing issue ~1 year ago for a couple days; no hospitalizations or injections noted.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: not documented.
  - Current medications: not documented.
- Social context:
  - Not stated.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression:
  - Unilateral left-ear hearing loss with tinnitus and intermittent dizziness; not acutely ill.
  - Plan to exclude cerumen impaction with otoscopy and assess tympanic membrane; tinnitus explained as a common but not fully understood phenomenon.
  - Possible involvement of inner ear/balance system or other ENT etiologies to be explored after ear examination.
  - Not an emergency; further evaluation pending with primary care ENT assessment.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advised:
  - Schedule face-to-face ear/otology assessment with a GP within roughly 4–5 days (not an emergency).
  - GP visit will include an ear exam to determine wax blockage or other pathology.
  - The patient will be contacted by admin to slot the appointment.
  - If any issues arise before the appointment, the patient is advised to book another appointment (video consult available).
- Patient/caregiver instructions:
  - Read the tinnitus leaflet linked in the notes prior to the appointment.
  - Attend the scheduled ear examination; findings will guide next steps.
- Escalation criteria/red flags:
  - Not specified in the transcript beyond the general instruction to seek follow-up if problems arise before the appointment.
- Follow-up:
  - Post-exam plan to determine next steps (possible ENT/allergy referral or further management) after ear examination.
  - Notes and plan will be available to the GP who performs the examination.

  - Allergy list (not documented).

  - Objective ear exam findings (otoscopic results, tympanic membrane status) and audiology results (not available in transcript).
